interest: Shows 1937 German-Japanese naval courtesies after the Anti-Comintern Pact, including a Hitler audience and rare access to German industrial plants.
overview: 1937 reports: the cruiser Ashigara's Kiel/Berlin visit brought a Hitler audience, Raeder-hosted receptions, armed marchers at Skagerrak Day, and unusual access to restricted German plants, signaling Anti-Comintern Pact intelligence cooperation.

people.name: Erich Raeder
people.role: Admiral and Commander-in-Chief of the German Navy

subfiles.about: A U.S. Naval Attaché intelligence report describing the extraordinary official, ceremonial, and industrial courtesies extended by the German government to the officers and crew of the Japanese cruiser Ashigara.
subfiles.summary: Report: the cruiser Ashigara's crew got a Hitler audience, Raeder-hosted events, and rare access to restricted German plants in 1937.
subfiles.title: Naval Attaché's Report on German-Japanese Relations and Courtesies Extended to the Japanese Cruiser Ashigara
subfiles.to: Chief of Naval Operations, Navy Department

subfiles.about: A State Department cross-reference sheet indexing a prior naval attaché report regarding visits of Japanese naval vessels to German ports.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to a May 1937 attaché report on the Japanese cruiser Ashigara's visit to German ports.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet for Report R-561 on Visit of Japanese Naval Vessels to German Ports
